free_tier.stated: No free plan. The pricing page shows the 1-year plan at '$ 4.00 / month', '$ 96.00' struck through and 'Total $ 48.00', plus a 7-day free trial that is 'only available with certain payment types and providers' and cannot be activated with cryptocurrency. The pricing page lists no other term.
free_tier.notes: The trial is 7 days; the unit vocabulary has no days term, so mixed is used. The page lists one plan length only (1 year). A September 2026 vendor post says a 6-month plan was being added and the 2-year plan retired; the 6-month and monthly prices are not on the page read.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: No byte cap is stated on the pricing page ('All features on all plans', 'No logs, no ads, no tracking'). A vendor support page says Anonymous mode (5 hops) 'is not designed for high-volume transfers' and recommends Fast mode (2-hop WireGuard) for large downloads.
egress.free_allowance: none: no free plan; a 7-day trial exists

interface_detail: A tunnel with apps and a command-line client, nym-vpnc. Protocols: AmneziaWG (a WireGuard fork) in Fast mode, which the vendor states is the only VPN protocol, and the Nym mixnet in Anonymous mode; OpenVPN and IKEv2/IPSec are not supported. UDP: unverified: no page read names the transport. Port forwarding: unverified: no page read states it. SOCKS5: the command-line client has 'nym-vpnc socks5 enable' and the docs say NymVPN can expose a local SOCKS5 proxy; it is a local listener, not a hosted endpoint. Obfuscation: AmneziaWG sends decoy packets before the handshake. BitTorrent: supported; exit operators in some countries may block it.
tooling: The vendor's apps and its nym-vpnc command-line client (tunnel set --two-hop on selects 2-hop WireGuard; socks5 enable exposes a local SOCKS5 proxy). No hosted SOCKS5 endpoint is documented in the pages read.
chaining: A tunnel exit with two modes: 2-hop WireGuard for throughput and a 5-hop mixnet for metadata protection; the upstream sees the exit gateway's address.

limits.value: exit gateways are run by independent operators; the support page says operators in countries where torrenting is restricted may block P2P on their exit, so reachability depends on the exit chosen

limits_note: Concurrent use is capped at 10 devices per account on the pricing page; the vocabulary has no kind for it. Anonymous mode is not designed for high-volume transfers (vendor wording), so throughput depends on the mode.
binding_note: No byte quota or request rate is published; the stated caveats are the mode (Anonymous mode is not for large transfers) and exit-operator policy, neither of which the limit vocabulary names.

identity_cost.detail: The home page says NymVPN is accessed 'with an anonymous 24-word passphrase, nothing else'. A later release adds optional social logins through Privy while the passphrase login remains. Paying by card goes through Stripe, and the 7-day trial needs a payment method; cryptocurrency, Monero, Zcash, GNU Taler and cash are listed as payment options.

reliability_note: Exit servers are run by independent operators and a restricted-country operator may block P2P on its exit; the fix the vendor gives is to switch exit location and reconnect.
confidence_note: Documented: price, trial, protocol, SOCKS5 and BitTorrent lines are quoted from the vendor's pricing page, support articles and docs. Nothing was connected through the service. UDP and port forwarding are unverified because no first-party page read states them.
price_per_tb_month: USD 48 total for 1 year (USD 4.00 a month shown); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
